## Parameters and Conversions
```{python}
# Conversions

cm2_ha = 100000000 # 100,000,000 cm2 = 1 ha

cm3_gal = 3785.41 # 3785.41 cm2 = 1 Gal

m3_kGal = 3.785411784

gal_acre_ft = 325851 # 1 acre ft = 325851 gallons

acre_ha = 2.47105 # 1 hectare = 2.47105 acres

cm_ft = 30.48 # 1 ft = 30.48 cm

cm_in = 2.54

lb_tonne = 2204.62

# Hours in a Month
hrs_month = 720

#Days in Month
days_month = 30

#Growing Season Months
gs_months = 9

# Parameters

ha = 200 # hectares average size of texas farms 411 acres rounded up, https://www.texasagriculture.gov/About/TexasAgStats.aspx#:~:text=For%2036%25%20of%20producers%20in,by%2012%20acres%20from%202012.

price = 200 # $/ metric ton #https://www.indexmundi.com/commodities/?commodity=wheat

#note $ /acre ranges from $7-85 / acre assuming only a few cm of depth similiar price to irrigation water 


#Water production cost $2 / Gal convert to $ / cm
cost_alt_water = 2 / 365 / cm3_gal * cm2_ha * ha


# 6.25 kWh / kGal > / Gal > / acre-ft > acre-cm > / ha-cm > kwh/cm
alt_water_elc = 6.25 / 1000 * gal_acre_ft / cm_ft * acre_ha * ha







# Irrigation Water Cost https://news.berkeley.edu/berkeley_blog/the-cost-of-irrigation-water-and-urban-farming/
#  Given in $ / cm from: $ 40 / acre-ft / gal_acre_ft / cm3_gal * cm2_ha * ha 

#cost_irrigation_water = 40 / gal_acre_ft / cm3_gal * cm2_ha * ha  # $ / cm 


# $7 / ac- in convert to $ / cm
cost_irrigation_water =  7 / cm_in * acre_ha * ha

# $10 / ac- in convert to $ / cm
cost_op_alt_water =  10 / cm_in * acre_ha * ha


# 1 kWh / kGal
irrigation_water_elc = 1 / 1000 * gal_acre_ft / cm_ft * acre_ha * ha


salt_conc = 2 # deciSiemens / meter = dS/m

salt_conc_water = 1 # deciSiemens / meter = dS/m

precip = 20 * cm_in # 20 inches of rain


 #  1.5 acre-ft / acre / yr halved for season https://www.nass.usda.gov/Publications/Highlights/2019/2017Census_Irrigation_and_WaterManagement.pdf
 
irrigation_water_limit = 0.25

max_irrigation_water = irrigation_water_limit * cm_ft 

# $ / kW of capacity
cost_alt_elc = 1500



cost_utility_elc = 0.08



#Renewable Energy

# Capacity Factor Solar https://pv-magazine-usa.com/2018/07/03/texas-getting-315-mw-of-solar-power/

cf_solar = 0.30

# Fu, R., Feldman, D., Margolis, R., 2018. U.S. Solar Photovoltaic System Cost Benchmark: Q1 2018. Tech. rep., National Renewable Energy Laboratory, Golden, CO.

solar_dollar_kW = 1500

# wInd Costs https://www.energy.gov/sites/prod/files/2019/08/f65/2018%20Wind%20Technologies%20Market%20Report%20FINAL.pdf

wind_dollar_kW = 840
```
## The Effect of Water on Profit and Crop Growth

```{python}

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

water = np.array(range(120))


# From Dinar et. al 1991 "Production functions relating crop yield, water quality and quantity, soil salinity and drainage volume"

y1 = (-3.350 + 0.2064*water - 0.0014*water*water + 
               3.555 * salt_conc_water + 2.326 * salt_conc_water*salt_conc_water 
               -2.031 * salt_conc + 0.823 * salt_conc*salt_conc
               -0.071 * water * salt_conc_water + 0.033 * water * salt_conc 
               -2.754 * salt_conc_water * salt_conc)

p1 = (y1*price*10 )

fig, ax = plt.subplots()

ax.plot(water,p1, label = 'Profit', color = 'red') # profit is red line
ax.set_title('Profit and Yield by Water Depth')
ax.set_xlabel('Water Depth (cm)')
ax.set_ylabel('Profit ($/10 ha)')
ax.set_ylim([-100,7200])
ax.grid(True)
ax.legend(loc = 'lower right')

ax2 = ax.twinx()
ax2.plot(water,y1*lb_tonne, label = 'Yield') # yield is blue line
ax2.set_ylabel('Yield (tonnes/ha)')
ax.set_ylim([-100,8500])
ax2.legend()
plt.show()




```

# Run with equal probablity of wet, dry, dry-moderate, and moderate climates


```{python, include = F}


import gurobipy as gp

m = gp.Model()

#m.params.NonConvex = 2 # Says its non convex but it is (FIXED quadratic constraints can't be equality)

# Set to maximize
m.ModelSense = -1

# Add variables

#First Stage Decision Variables Strategic Investment Decisions, pick what climate you are in which automatically picks how much alternative water to invest in

alt_water_cap = m.addVar(name = 'alt_water_cap', lb = 0) # cm of depth
alt_elc_cap = m.addVar(name = 'alt_elc_cap', lb = 0) # kW of depth


#Second Stage Decision Variables Operational Decisions, Pick how much water to use and how much irrigation water to buy

# Change these variables to be a function of option, climate, and season
water = m.addVars(run_c0, year, lb = 0, name = 'water') # water used for crop, cm of depth
irrigation_water = m.addVars(run_c0, year, lb = 0, ub = max_irrigation_water, name = 'irrigation_water') # cm of depth
alt_water = m.addVars(run_c0, year, lb = 0, name = 'alt_water') # alt_water used for crop, cm of depth
alt_elc = m.addVars(run_c0, year, lb = 0, name = 'alt_elc') # alt_elc to power water, kWh
utility_elc = m.addVars(run_c0, year, lb = 0, name = 'util_elc') # util_elc to power water, kWh
elc = m.addVars(run_c0, year, lb = 0, name = 'elc') # total elc to power water, kWh

#Functions of the Above, also functions of option, climate, and season, 
crop_yield = m.addVars(run_c0, year, lb = 0, name = 'yield') # tonne/ha
profit = m.addVars(run_c0, obj = 1/samples_c0, name = 'profit') # $



# Objective



m.addConstrs( (profit[r] == crop_yield.sum(r,'*') * ha * price +
              -alt_water_cap * cost_alt_water  +
              -irrigation_water.sum(r,'*') * cost_irrigation_water +
              -alt_elc_cap * cost_alt_elc +
              -utility_elc.sum(r,'*') * cost_utility_elc
              for r in run_c0)
            ,name = 'profit_constr')

# Water Equations

m.addConstrs( (alt_water[r,y] <= alt_water_cap
               for r in run_c0 for y in year)
             ,name = 'water_cap' )
 

m.addConstrs( (rain_c0_dict[r,y] + alt_water[r,y] + irrigation_water[r,y] >= water[r,y]
              for r in run_c0 for y in year)
             ,name = 'water' )
             
             
#Energy for Alt Water Equations    

m.addConstrs( (alt_water[r,y] * alt_water_elc + irrigation_water[r,y] * irrigation_water_elc <= elc[r,y]
               for r in run_c0 for y in year)
             ,name = 'elc_water' )

# Energy Capacity and Balance Equations

m.addConstrs( (alt_elc[r,y] <= alt_elc_cap * cf_solar * hrs_month * gs_months
               for r in run_c0 for y in year)
             ,name = 'elc_cap' )




m.addConstrs( (alt_elc[r,y] + utility_elc[r,y] >= elc[r,y]
               for r in run_c0 for y in year)
             ,name = 'elc_balance' )





for r in run_c0:
    for y in year :
            m.addQConstr( (crop_yield[r,y] <= -3.350 + 0.2064*water[r,y]  - 0.0014*water[r,y]*water[r,y]  + 
               3.555 * salt_conc_water + 2.326 * salt_conc_water*salt_conc_water +
               -2.031 * salt_conc + 0.823 * salt_conc*salt_conc +
               -0.071 * water[r,y]  * salt_conc_water + 0.033 * water[r,y]  * salt_conc +
               -2.754 * salt_conc_water * salt_conc
               )
               , name = 'crop_yield' )


m.update();



```

```{python}
import numpy as np
import scipy.stats as scs

# Calculating Confidence Interval

profit_array = np.array(list(profit_dict.values()))

crop_yield_array = np.fromiter(crop_yield_dict.values(), dtype=float)


# rename profit array
a = profit_array * 1.0

# number of samples in array
n = len(a)
# calculate mean and sample error
m, se = np.mean(a), scs.sem(a)
# calculate t distrb
t = scs.t.ppf((1 + 0.95) / 2., n-1)
# calculate step size
h = se * t
# print sample size, mean, standard error, t value, step size, lower interval, and higher interval
n, m, se, t, h, m-h, m+h

# rename crop yield array
b = crop_yield_array * 1.0

# number of samples in array
n = len(b)
# calculate mean and sample error
m, se = np.mean(b), scs.sem(b)
# calculate t distrb
t = scs.t.ppf((1 + 0.95) / 2., n-1)
# calculate step size
h = se * t
# print sample size, mean, standard error, t value, step size, lower interval, and higher interval
n, m, se, t, h, m-h, m+h
```

## Climate 1 Problem and Solution

```{python, include = F}


import gurobipy as gp



m = gp.Model()

#m.params.NonConvex = 2 # Says its non convex but it is (FIXED quadratic constraints can't be equality)

# Set to maximize
m.ModelSense = -1

# Add variables

#First Stage Decision Variables Strategic Investment Decisions, pick what climate you are in which automatically picks how much alternative water to invest in

alt_water_cap = m.addVar(name = 'alt_water_cap', lb = 0) # cm of depth
alt_elc_cap = m.addVar(name = 'alt_elc_cap', lb = 0) # kW of depth


#Second Stage Decision Variables Operational Decisions, Pick how much water to use and how much irrigation water to buy

# Change these variables to be a function of option, climate, and season
water = m.addVars(run_c1, year, lb = 0, name = 'water') # water used for crop, cm of depth
irrigation_water = m.addVars(run_c1, year, lb = 0, ub = max_irrigation_water, name = 'irrigation_water') # cm of depth
alt_water = m.addVars(run_c1, year, lb = 0, name = 'alt_water') # alt_water used for crop, cm of depth
alt_elc = m.addVars(run_c1, year, lb = 0, name = 'alt_elc') # alt_elc to power water, kWh
utility_elc = m.addVars(run_c1, year, lb = 0, name = 'util_elc') # util_elc to power water, kWh
elc = m.addVars(run_c1, year, lb = 0, name = 'elc') # total elc to power water, kWh

#Functions of the Above, also functions of option, climate, and season, 
crop_yield = m.addVars(run_c1, year, lb = 0, name = 'yield') # tonne/ha
profit = m.addVars(run_c1, obj = 1/samples_c1, name = 'profit') # $



#Maybe add a new profit variable that is the sum of the profit based on climate for easy coefficients



# Objective


m.addConstrs( (profit[r] == crop_yield.sum(r,'*') * ha * price +
              -alt_water_cap * cost_alt_water  +
              -irrigation_water.sum(r,'*') * cost_irrigation_water +
              -alt_elc_cap * cost_alt_elc +
              -utility_elc.sum(r,'*') * cost_utility_elc
              for r in run_c1)
            ,name = 'profit_constr')

# Water Equations

m.addConstrs( (alt_water[r,y] <= alt_water_cap
               for r in run_c1 for y in year)
             ,name = 'water_cap' )
 

m.addConstrs( (rain_c1[r,y] + alt_water[r,y] + irrigation_water[r,y] >= water[r,y]
              for r in run_c1 for y in year)
             ,name = 'water' )
             
             
#Energy for Alt Water Equations    

m.addConstrs( alt_water[r,y] * alt_water_elc + irrigation_water[r,y] * irrigation_water_elc <= elc[r,y]
               for r in run_c1 for y in year)
             ,name = 'elc_water' )

# Energy Capacity and Balance Equations

m.addConstrs( (alt_elc[r,y] <= alt_elc_cap * cf_solar * hrs_month * gs_months
               for r in run_c1 for y in year)
             ,name = 'elc_cap' )




m.addConstrs( alt_elc[r,y] + utility_elc[r,y] >= elc[r,y]
               for r in run_c1 for y in year)
             ,name = 'elc_balance' )





for r in run_c1:
    for y in year :
            m.addQConstr( (crop_yield[r,y] <= -3.350 + 0.2064*water[r,y]  - 0.0014*water[r,y]*water[r,y]  + 
               3.555 * salt_conc_water + 2.326 * salt_conc_water*salt_conc_water +
               -2.031 * salt_conc + 0.823 * salt_conc*salt_conc +
               -0.071 * water[r,y]  * salt_conc_water + 0.033 * water[r,y]  * salt_conc +
               -2.754 * salt_conc_water * salt_conc
               )
               , name = 'crop_yield' )


m.update();



```

```{python}
alt_water_c1
```

## C0 realized in Climate 1 Problem and Solution

```{python, include = F}


import gurobipy as gp

m = gp.Model()

#m.params.NonConvex = 2 # Says its non convex but it is (FIXED quadratic constraints can't be equality)

# Set to maximize
m.ModelSense = -1

# Add variables

#First Stage Decision Variables Strategic Investment Decisions, pick what climate you are in which automatically picks how much alternative water to invest in

alt_water_cap = alt_water_c0
alt_elc_cap = alt_elc_c0
#alt_water_cap = m.addVar(name = 'alt_water_cap', lb = 0) # cm of depth
#alt_elc_cap = m.addVar(name = 'alt_elc_cap', lb = 0) # kW of depth


#Second Stage Decision Variables Operational Decisions, Pick how much water to use and how much irrigation water to buy

# Change these variables to be a function of option, climate, and season
water = m.addVars(run_c1, year, lb = 0, name = 'water') # water used for crop, cm of depth
irrigation_water = m.addVars(run_c1, year, lb = 0, ub = max_irrigation_water, name = 'irrigation_water') # cm of depth
alt_water = m.addVars(run_c1, year, lb = 0, name = 'alt_water') # alt_water used for crop, cm of depth
alt_elc = m.addVars(run_c1, year, lb = 0, name = 'alt_elc') # alt_elc to power water, kWh
utility_elc = m.addVars(run_c1, year, lb = 0, name = 'util_elc') # util_elc to power water, kWh
elc = m.addVars(run_c1, year, lb = 0, name = 'elc') # total elc to power water, kWh

#Functions of the Above, also functions of option, climate, and season, 
crop_yield = m.addVars(run_c1, year, lb = 0, name = 'yield') # tonne/ha
profit = m.addVars(run_c1, obj = 1/samples_c1, name = 'profit') # $



#Maybe add a new profit variable that is the sum of the profit based on climate for easy coefficients



# Objective


m.addConstrs( (profit[r] == crop_yield.sum(r,'*') * ha * price +
              -alt_water_cap * cost_alt_water  +
              -irrigation_water.sum(r,'*') * cost_irrigation_water +
              -alt_elc_cap * cost_alt_elc +
              -utility_elc.sum(r,'*') * cost_utility_elc
              for r in run_c1)
            ,name = 'profit_constr')

# Water Equations

m.addConstrs( (alt_water[r,y] <= alt_water_cap
               for r in run_c1 for y in year)
             ,name = 'water_cap' )
 

m.addConstrs( (rain_c1[r,y] + alt_water[r,y] + irrigation_water[r,y] >= water[r,y]
              for r in run_c1 for y in year)
             ,name = 'water' )
             
             
#Energy for Alt Water Equations    

m.addConstrs( (alt_water[r,y] * alt_water_elc + irrigation_water[r,y] * irrigation_water_elc <= elc[r,y]
               for r in run_c1 for y in year)
             ,name = 'elc_water' )

# Energy Capacity and Balance Equations

m.addConstrs( (alt_elc[r,y] <= alt_elc_cap * cf_solar * hrs_month * gs_months
               for r in run_c1 for y in year)
             ,name = 'elc_cap' )




m.addConstrs( (alt_elc[r,y] + utility_elc[r,y] >= elc[r,y]
               for r in run_c1 for y in year)
             ,name = 'elc_balance' )





for r in run_c1:
    for y in year :
            m.addQConstr( (crop_yield[r,y] <= -3.350 + 0.2064*water[r,y]  - 0.0014*water[r,y]*water[r,y]  + 
               3.555 * salt_conc_water + 2.326 * salt_conc_water*salt_conc_water +
               -2.031 * salt_conc + 0.823 * salt_conc*salt_conc +
               -0.071 * water[r,y]  * salt_conc_water + 0.033 * water[r,y]  * salt_conc +
               -2.754 * salt_conc_water * salt_conc
               )
               , name = 'crop_yield' )


m.update();


```

```{python}
m.optimize()
obj = m.getObjective()
print('Objective Function')
print(obj.getValue())



```

```{python, include = F}


import gurobipy as gp



m = gp.Model()

#m.params.NonConvex = 2 # Says its non convex but it is (FIXED quadratic constraints can't be equality)

# Set to maximize
m.ModelSense = -1

alt_water_cap = m.addVar(name = 'alt_water_cap', lb = 0) # cm of depth
alt_elc_cap = m.addVar(name = 'alt_elc_cap', lb = 0) # kW of depth


#Second Stage Decision Variables Operational Decisions, Pick how much water to use and how much irrigation water to buy

# Change these variables to be a function of option, climate, and season
water = m.addVars(run_c2, year, lb = 0, name = 'water') # water used for crop, cm of depth
irrigation_water = m.addVars(run_c2, year, lb = 0, ub = max_irrigation_water, name = 'irrigation_water') # cm of depth
alt_water = m.addVars(run_c2, year, lb = 0, name = 'alt_water') # alt_water used for crop, cm of depth
alt_elc = m.addVars(run_c2, year, lb = 0, name = 'alt_elc') # alt_elc to power water, kWh
utility_elc = m.addVars(run_c2, year, lb = 0, name = 'util_elc') # util_elc to power water, kWh
elc = m.addVars(run_c2, year, lb = 0, name = 'elc') # total elc to power water, kWh

#Functions of the Above, also functions of option, climate, and season, 
crop_yield = m.addVars(run_c2, year, lb = 0, name = 'yield') # tonne/ha
profit = m.addVars(run_c2, obj = 1/samples_c2, name = 'profit') # $



#Maybe add a new profit variable that is the sum of the profit based on climate for easy coefficients



# Objective


m.addConstrs( (profit[r] == crop_yield.sum(r,'*') * ha * price +
              -alt_water_cap * cost_alt_water  +
              -irrigation_water.sum(r,'*') * cost_irrigation_water +
              -alt_elc_cap * cost_alt_elc +
              -utility_elc.sum(r,'*') * cost_utility_elc
              for r in run_c2)
            ,name = 'profit_constr')

# Water Equations

m.addConstrs( (alt_water[r,y] <= alt_water_cap
               for r in run_c2 for y in year)
             ,name = 'water_cap' )
 

m.addConstrs( (rain_c2[r,y] + alt_water[r,y] + irrigation_water[r,y] >= water[r,y]
              for r in run_c2 for y in year)
             ,name = 'water' )
             
             
#Energy for Alt Water Equations    

m.addConstrs( alt_water[r,y] * alt_water_elc + irrigation_water[r,y] * irrigation_water_elc <= elc[r,y]
               for r in run_c2 for y in year)
             ,name = 'elc_water' )

# Energy Capacity and Balance Equations

m.addConstrs( (alt_elc[r,y] <= alt_elc_cap * cf_solar * hrs_month * gs_months
               for r in run_c2 for y in year)
             ,name = 'elc_cap' )




m.addConstrs( alt_elc[r,y] + utility_elc[r,y] >= elc[r,y]
               for r in run_c2 for y in year)
             ,name = 'elc_balance' )





for r in run_c2:
    for y in year :
            m.addQConstr( (crop_yield[r,y] <= -3.350 + 0.2064*water[r,y]  - 0.0014*water[r,y]*water[r,y]  + 
               3.555 * salt_conc_water + 2.326 * salt_conc_water*salt_conc_water +
               -2.031 * salt_conc + 0.823 * salt_conc*salt_conc +
               -0.071 * water[r,y]  * salt_conc_water + 0.033 * water[r,y]  * salt_conc +
               -2.754 * salt_conc_water * salt_conc
               )
               , name = 'crop_yield' )


m.update();
```

## Climate 3 Problem and Solution

```{python, include = F}


import gurobipy as gp



m = gp.Model()

#m.params.NonConvex = 2 # Says its non convex but it is (FIXED quadratic constraints can't be equality)

# Set to maximize
m.ModelSense = -1

# Add variables

#First Stage Decision Variables Strategic Investment Decisions, pick what climate you are in which automatically picks how much alternative water to invest in

alt_water_cap = m.addVar(name = 'alt_water_cap', lb = 0) # cm of depth
alt_elc_cap = m.addVar(name = 'alt_elc_cap', lb = 0) # kW of depth


#Second Stage Decision Variables Operational Decisions, Pick how much water to use and how much irrigation water to buy

# Change these variables to be a function of option, climate, and season
water = m.addVars(run_c3, year, lb = 0, name = 'water') # water used for crop, cm of depth
irrigation_water = m.addVars(run_c3, year, lb = 0, ub = max_irrigation_water, name = 'irrigation_water') # cm of depth
alt_water = m.addVars(run_c3, year, lb = 0, name = 'alt_water') # alt_water used for crop, cm of depth
alt_elc = m.addVars(run_c3, year, lb = 0, name = 'alt_elc') # alt_elc to power water, kWh
utility_elc = m.addVars(run_c3, year, lb = 0, name = 'util_elc') # util_elc to power water, kWh
elc = m.addVars(run_c3, year, lb = 0, name = 'elc') # total elc to power water, kWh

#Functions of the Above, also functions of option, climate, and season, 
crop_yield = m.addVars(run_c3, year, lb = 0, name = 'yield') # tonne/ha
profit = m.addVars(run_c3, obj = 1/samples_c3, name = 'profit') # $



#Maybe add a new profit variable that is the sum of the profit based on climate for easy coefficients



# Objective


m.addConstrs( (profit[r] == crop_yield.sum(r,'*') * ha * price +
              -alt_water_cap * cost_alt_water  +
              -irrigation_water.sum(r,'*') * cost_irrigation_water +
              -alt_elc_cap * cost_alt_elc +
              -utility_elc.sum(r,'*') * cost_utility_elc
              for r in run_c3)
            ,name = 'profit_constr')

# Water Equations

m.addConstrs( (alt_water[r,y] <= alt_water_cap
               for r in run_c3 for y in year)
             ,name = 'water_cap' )
 

m.addConstrs( (rain_c3[r,y] + alt_water[r,y] + irrigation_water[r,y] >= water[r,y]
              for r in run_c3 for y in year)
             ,name = 'water' )
             
             
#Energy for Alt Water Equations    

m.addConstrs( alt_water[r,y] * alt_water_elc + irrigation_water[r,y] * irrigation_water_elc <= elc[r,y]
               for r in run_c3 for y in year)
             ,name = 'elc_water' )

# Energy Capacity and Balance Equations

m.addConstrs( (alt_elc[r,y] <= alt_elc_cap * cf_solar * hrs_month * gs_months
               for r in run_c3 for y in year)
             ,name = 'elc_cap' )




m.addConstrs( alt_elc[r,y] + utility_elc[r,y] >= elc[r,y]
               for r in run_c3 for y in year)
             ,name = 'elc_balance' )





for r in run_c3:
    for y in year :
            m.addQConstr( (crop_yield[r,y] <= -3.350 + 0.2064*water[r,y]  - 0.0014*water[r,y]*water[r,y]  + 
               3.555 * salt_conc_water + 2.326 * salt_conc_water*salt_conc_water +
               -2.031 * salt_conc + 0.823 * salt_conc*salt_conc +
               -0.071 * water[r,y]  * salt_conc_water + 0.033 * water[r,y]  * salt_conc +
               -2.754 * salt_conc_water * salt_conc
               )
               , name = 'crop_yield' )


m.update();



```

```{python}
m.optimize()
obj = m.getObjective()
alt_water_c3 = alt_water_cap.X
alt_elc_c3 = alt_elc_cap.X
print('Objective Function')
print(obj.getValue())
print('Alt Water Investment')
alt_water_c3
print('Alt ELC Investment')
alt_elc_c3


```

```{python, include = F}
# Add variables

#First Stage Decision Variables Strategic Investment Decisions, pick what climate you are in which automatically picks how much alternative water to invest in

alt_water_cap = alt_water_c0
alt_elc_cap = alt_elc_c0
#alt_water_cap = m.addVar(name = 'alt_water_cap', lb = 0) # cm of depth
#alt_elc_cap = m.addVar(name = 'alt_elc_cap', lb = 0) # kW of depth


#Second Stage Decision Variables Operational Decisions, Pick how much water to use and how much irrigation water to buy

# Change these variables to be a function of option, climate, and season
water = m.addVars(run_c4, year, lb = 0, name = 'water') # water used for crop, cm of depth
irrigation_water = m.addVars(run_c4, year, lb = 0, ub = max_irrigation_water, name = 'irrigation_water') # cm of depth
alt_water = m.addVars(run_c4, year, lb = 0, name = 'alt_water') # alt_water used for crop, cm of depth
alt_elc = m.addVars(run_c4, year, lb = 0, name = 'alt_elc') # alt_elc to power water, kWh
utility_elc = m.addVars(run_c4, year, lb = 0, name = 'util_elc') # util_elc to power water, kWh
elc = m.addVars(run_c4, year, lb = 0, name = 'elc') # total elc to power water, kWh

#Functions of the Above, also functions of option, climate, and season, 
crop_yield = m.addVars(run_c4, year, lb = 0, name = 'yield') # tonne/ha
profit = m.addVars(run_c4, obj = 1/samples_c4, name = 'profit') # $



#Maybe add a new profit variable that is the sum of the profit based on climate for easy coefficients



# Objective


m.addConstrs( (profit[r] == crop_yield.sum(r,'*') * ha * price +
              -alt_water_cap * cost_alt_water  +
              -irrigation_water.sum(r,'*') * cost_irrigation_water +
              -alt_elc_cap * cost_alt_elc +
              -utility_elc.sum(r,'*') * cost_utility_elc
              for r in run_c4)
            ,name = 'profit_constr')

# Water Equations

m.addConstrs( (alt_water[r,y] <= alt_water_cap
               for r in run_c4 for y in year)
             ,name = 'water_cap' )
 

m.addConstrs( (rain_c4[r,y] + alt_water[r,y] + irrigation_water[r,y] >= water[r,y]
              for r in run_c4 for y in year)
             ,name = 'water' )
             
             
#Energy for Alt Water Equations    

m.addConstrs( (alt_water[r,y] * alt_water_elc + irrigation_water[r,y] * irrigation_water_elc <= elc[r,y]
               for r in run_c4 for y in year)
             ,name = 'elc_water' )

# Energy Capacity and Balance Equations

m.addConstrs( (alt_elc[r,y] <= alt_elc_cap * cf_solar * hrs_month * gs_months
               for r in run_c4 for y in year)
             ,name = 'elc_cap' )




m.addConstrs( (alt_elc[r,y] + utility_elc[r,y] >= elc[r,y]
               for r in run_c4 for y in year)
             ,name = 'elc_balance' )





for r in run_c4:
    for y in year :
            m.addQConstr( (crop_yield[r,y] <= -3.350 + 0.2064*water[r,y]  - 0.0014*water[r,y]*water[r,y]  + 
               3.555 * salt_conc_water + 2.326 * salt_conc_water*salt_conc_water +
               -2.031 * salt_conc + 0.823 * salt_conc*salt_conc +
               -0.071 * water[r,y]  * salt_conc_water + 0.033 * water[r,y]  * salt_conc +
               -2.754 * salt_conc_water * salt_conc
               )
               , name = 'crop_yield' )


m.update();


```

```{python}
m.optimize()
obj = m.getObjective()
print('Objective Function')
print(obj.getValue())



```

```{r}
                   alt_water = alt_water_c4 %>% group_by(year) %>% summarize(water_depth = mean(water_depth))  %>% select(water_depth) %>% pull(water_depth),
                   alt_elc = alt_elc_c4 %>% group_by(year) %>% summarize(elc_prod = mean(elc_prod))  %>% select(elc_prod) %>% pull(elc_prod),
                   
                   irrigation_water = irrigation_c4 %>% group_by(year) %>% summarize(water_depth = mean(water_depth))  %>% select(water_depth) %>% pull(water_depth),  
                   utility_elc = utility_elc_c4 %>% group_by(year) %>% summarize(elc_prod = mean(elc_prod)) %>% select(elc_prod) %>% pull(elc_prod), 
                   total_water = water_c4 %>% group_by(year) %>% summarize(water_depth = mean(water_depth)) %>% select(water_depth) %>% pull(water_depth),   
                   total_elc = elc_c4 %>% group_by(year) %>% summarize(elc_prod = mean(elc_prod)) %>% select(elc_prod) %>% pull(elc_prod),
                   
                   precip = precips_c4_tbl %>% group_by(year) %>% summarize(precip = mean(precip)) %>% select(precip) %>% pull(precip),
                scenario = 'Dry_Climate') %>% 
  mutate_if(is.numeric, funs(round(.,2)))



c04_df <- tibble(Year = seq(1,25), 
                   crop_yield = crop_yield_c04 %>% group_by(year) %>% summarize(crop_yield = mean(crop_yield))  %>% select(crop_yield) %>% pull(crop_yield), 
                   alt_water = alt_water_c04 %>% group_by(year) %>% summarize(water_depth = mean(water_depth))  %>% select(water_depth) %>% pull(water_depth),
                   alt_elc = alt_elc_c04 %>% group_by(year) %>% summarize(elc_prod = mean(elc_prod))  %>% select(elc_prod) %>% pull(elc_prod),
                   
                   irrigation_water = irrigation_c04 %>% group_by(year) %>% summarize(water_depth = mean(water_depth))  %>% select(water_depth) %>% pull(water_depth),  
                   utility_elc = utility_elc_c04 %>% group_by(year) %>% summarize(elc_prod = mean(elc_prod)) %>% select(elc_prod) %>% pull(elc_prod), 
                   total_water = water_c04 %>% group_by(year) %>% summarize(water_depth = mean(water_depth)) %>% select(water_depth) %>% pull(water_depth),   
                   total_elc = elc_c04 %>% group_by(year) %>% summarize(elc_prod = mean(elc_prod)) %>% select(elc_prod) %>% pull(elc_prod),
                   
                   precip = precips_c4_tbl %>% group_by(year) %>% summarize(precip = mean(precip)) %>% select(precip) %>% pull(precip),
                 
                 scenario = 'Dry_Climate_Realized') %>% mutate_if(is.numeric, funs(round(.,2)))





stochvclimate4_df <- rbind(stoch_df,c4_df,c04_df)


stochvclimate4_df
```
